ai.purpose: RTT/1 engine layer for Information Theory: operator grammar, entropy behavior, channel structure, and minimal coherence examples.

engine.description: Defines the operator grammar and dimensional behavior of distinctions, entropy, and channels within the RTT substrate.

entropy.description: Measures uncertainty or indistinguishability across possible states.

mutual_information.description: Measures shared distinctions between two variables or channels.

channel_capacity.description: Defines the maximum rate at which distinctions can be transmitted reliably.

encoding.description: Maps distinctions into codewords under constraints.

redundancy.description: Adds structure to protect distinctions from noise.

signal_alphabet.description: Defines the set of distinguishable symbols available for encoding.

dimensional_mapping.R0: Pure distinctions; entropy and codes defined without physical substrate.
dimensional_mapping.R1: Primitive channels; minimal signal carriers and noise.
dimensional_mapping.R2: Physical, biological, or computational implementations of codes and channels.
dimensional_mapping.R3: Complex multi-channel systems with stable error correction and redundancy.

integration.notes: RTT/1 treats Information Theory as a distinction-first grammar; deeper resonance and substrate integration occur in RTT/2 and RTT/3.
